AttentionBlocker.description:
One reason a ``needs_attention`` run may not simply be reopened — a derived
view (folded from the journal), never persisted.

``kind`` is ``counter_capped_turn`` for a turn that burned its whole retry budget
and still has no completed record. A ``needs_attention`` run with *no* blockers was
halted by the driver (auth / repeated provider failure), which the journal cannot
prove fixed but which also leaves nothing in the run itself to clear — so it
reopens on the operator's logged reason alone.
AttentionBlocker.title: AttentionBlocker

a later lane resolves the concept.

get.description:
Validate a signed link, AUDIT-APPEND FIRST (fail closed), then stream the file.

Not matter-scoped in the path — the token carries the (matter, run, deliverable)
audience. The access audit MUST record before a byte streams: if the audit write
fails, `AuditWriteError` propagates (500) and nothing is served (plan FD-3).

the current effective cap), reopening it for resumption (plan D5).

Reopen a ``needs_attention`` run once the operator has fixed what blocked it

verified Access email is the reopener recorded on the journal event.
